body:
Provenance today has three strong layers: the signature names the author key; the pool names
the last hop physically; the prefix is the receiver's petname. What is missing is custody in
time: nothing records when THIS delta stepped through the door. The channel record's
lastSyncedAt says when the door last opened, not what came through it.

Build: each sync that ACCEPTS deltas appends one receiver-signed arrival attestation into the
channel's pool — delta-ref pointers to the accepted deltas, the channel name, the peer address
(the channel's `from`), and the sync timestamp. Custody becomes data: it rides as-of reads
("what had arrived by Tuesday"), and it purges with the pool on drop, which is correct — the
trail was about the severed peer.

Judgment calls, settled:
- A sync that accepts NOTHING appends NOTHING. Liveness is already the channel record's job
  (lastSyncedAt); a per-poll heartbeat delta is delta soup by construction (compare kyber's D5:
  pulses are not facts). This is criterion (b), pinned two-sided.
- Pointer fan is capped at 256 refs per attestation; a larger batch appends ceil(N/256)
  attestations for that sync. An unbounded pointer list is an H8-shaped delta.
- The accepted-set seam: ground.federate returns a FederationReport of COUNTS only
  ({offered, accepted, rejected, held} — src/gateway/ingest.ts); the sync path holds no
  accepted-delta ids today. Extend the report ADDITIVELY to carry the accepted ids (preferred
  — diffing reactor snapshots around the call is O(store), an H8 shape the report extension
  avoids). Existing report consumers read counts and are unaffected.
- Vocabulary: a new `loam.arrival` context on the attestation's entity pointer, following the
  loam.binding-policy naming shape (src/gateway/binding-policy.ts is the pattern). Receiver-
  authored, so bindArrived's existing operator-author filter already excludes attestations from
  law consideration — assert it rather than assume it.

Acceptance criteria — federation tests in the existing memory-backend style:
(a) A sync accepting N>0 deltas appends exactly ceil(N/256) receiver-signed attestations in the
    pool, carrying the channel name, the from address, and delta-refs to each accepted delta.
    Verify: new test test/federation/arrival-attestations.test.ts.
(b) A sync accepting nothing appends NO ATTESTATION (two-sided, anti-soup). The fixture must
    isolate blessing side-effects: bindArrived blesses pool CONTENTS, not arrivals, so a
    resumed channel with pending rows can append manifest rows on an empty sync — use a quiet
    peer whose rows were already blessed by a prior sync, and assert no attestation-context
    delta lands (not a raw count). Verify: same file.
(c) Dropping the channel purges its attestations with the pool AND a bystander channel's
    attestations survive (two-sided erasure rail). Verify: same file.
(d) Attestations never bind as law and never re-export as blessings: a poll after attesting
    binds no new name (the recursive-blessing class stays dead). Verify: same file.
(e) An as-of read of the pool at a time between two syncs sees only the first sync's
    attestations. Verify: same file.

Merge tier: repair-shaped addition to the federation record — self-merges on the ordinary bar.
The admin delta view rides later; this ticket is the data.
title: Arrival attestations — custody as data, one signed stamp per sync
